security_audit.summary: All 82 static findings are false positives after contextual review. Most matches are Markdown backticks and instructional examples; the local validator uses quoted standard shell utilities without evaluating input as code. No prompt-injection attempt, data exfiltration intent, or malicious business logic was found.

remediation.issue: The local validator accepts a user-supplied filename and invokes standard utilities on it.
remediation.suggestion: Add -- before filename operands where supported and document that the validator reads only local agent files.

remediation.issue: Markdown backticks trigger many command-execution scanner matches.
remediation.suggestion: Tune static-analysis rules to distinguish fenced Markdown and inline code from executable shell contexts.

content.value_statement: Building a subagent can require careful decisions about triggers, tools, prompts, and output. This skill provides structured guidance, examples, and validation steps for dependable Claude Code agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required frontmatter fields for Claude Code subagent files.
Helps write focused system prompts with responsibilities and output expectations.
Recommends triggering descriptions and examples for appropriate agent selection.
Guides least-privilege tool selection for analysis, generation, and testing tasks.
Provides agent patterns for code review, testing, documentation, and security analysis.
Includes a local shell validator for agent file structure and basic content checks.
limitations: It does not automatically create, install, or publish an agent.
The validator checks structure and basic conventions, not agent quality or safety in every context.
Tool access recommendations require adaptation to the repository and organization policy.
Examples may need updates when Claude Code agent formats change.

use_cases.title: Create a review agent
use_cases.description: Define a focused code-review subagent with clear triggers, scoped tools, and a consistent findings format.

use_cases.title: Standardize team agents
use_cases.description: Create repeatable frontmatter and prompt conventions for a plugin or repository agent collection.

use_cases.title: Validate an agent file
use_cases.description: Check a draft agent file for required fields, frontmatter boundaries, and basic prompt expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Create a test agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a test-generation subagent for this repository. Propose its name, triggering description, tool scope, and system prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Improve triggers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this subagent description and examples. Rewrite them so Claude Code selects the agent only for API documentation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Apply least privilege
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent design and recommend the smallest tool set needed to inspect code and report security issues without modifying files.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Design an agent suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a small subagent suite for a TypeScript service. Define boundaries, triggers, tool scopes, handoff rules, and validation checks for each agent.

output_examples.input: Create a subagent that reviews pull requests for missing tests.
output: A focused agent name and selection description.
A read-only tool scope for source and test inspection.
A system prompt that prioritizes test gaps, impact, and actionable recommendations.
Required frontmatter fields and possible validation issues.
Suggested trigger examples for documentation requests.
A concise prompt outline with responsibilities and output expectations.

output_examples.input: Reduce permissions for a security analysis agent.
output: An explanation of which broad permissions are unnecessary.
A revised scope that preserves analysis capability.

best_practices: Give each agent one clear responsibility and explicit selection examples.
Grant only the tools required for the agent task and repository workflow.
Validate frontmatter and test the agent with representative user requests.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague names or descriptions that overlap with unrelated agents.
Do not grant full tool access when read-only or limited write access is sufficient.
Do not rely on a validator as the only review of agent behavior or permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design Claude Code subagents, including their metadata, prompts, triggers, examples, and tool scopes.

faq.question: Can it create an agent file for me?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and templates. You should review the generated file before adding it to your plugin or repository.

faq.question: Does the validator run an agent?
faq.answer: No. It checks local file structure and basic content conventions. It does not evaluate the agent response quality.

faq.question: How should I choose tools for an agent?
faq.answer: Start with the smallest set that supports the task. Add write or shell tools only when the agent genuinely needs them.

faq.question: Can I use this with Codex?
faq.answer: The guidance is useful for agent design, but its file format and examples target Claude Code plugins.

faq.question: How do I avoid incorrect agent triggering?
faq.answer: Use a specific description, include representative examples, and test the agent against both matching and nonmatching requests.
